newsitem.title: USA: China seen a key factor in future of copper market.
newsitem.headline: China seen a key factor in future of copper market.

text.p: Chinese activity is likely to be a key determinant in the copper market, particularly concerning the country's buying policy, analysts at an industry meeting said.
"China will be dominant for some years to come," Ted Arnold, first vice president and minerals economist at Merrill Lynch said.

There is a huge question mark over what the Strategic Reserve Bureau (SRB) will do, Arnold said at the American Metal Market forum here, adding that the SRB could buy an extra 100,000 tonnes of copper this year and 150,000 tonnes in 1998.
Jim Steele, Director of Research at Refco Inc, noted the increase in China's foreign reserves to $100.9 billion from the year-ago level of $74.7 billion.
"China has plenty of foreign exchange to buy copper or any other commodity purchase," Steele said.
China's activities and influence in the copper market will result in considerable price volatility at time, Arnold said.
"The Chinese and the SRB will be able to do things in copper that (Yasuo) Hamanaka coould only dream about...They will give Mr (David) King, LME Chief Executive, some problems," he said.
